newsitem.title: CYPRUS: CNN says Zaire rebel leader ready for talks.
newsitem.headline: CNN says Zaire rebel leader ready for talks.

text.p: Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila is prepared to enter into immediate negotiations and has dropped his demand for face-to-face talks with Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko, CNN reported on Tuesday.
The South African government, which has been in contact with both the rebels and government, "now believes Kabila would be ready to negotiate an immediate ceasefire," the network said.
A regional military source on Monday told Reuters the rebels were unlikely to agree to a ceasefire until they had irreversibly broken the back of Mobutu's government.

CNN, citing a South African government document, said that Kabila was willing to negotiate with representatives put forward by Mobutu, but was demanding the team have Mobutu's "mandate to negotiate and take decisions."

The rebel leader, whose troops now control more than a fifth of the giant Central Africa nation, will negotiate only once and says the talks must be "serious and arrive at a lasting political solution for Zaire," CNN reported.
He wants the talks to be held outside Zaire, preferably in South Africa, the network said.
It also said U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright had written to Mobutu asking him to nominate a person or team to negotiate with the rebels and to publicly state his commitment to the talks.

Mobutu's 32-year reign is looking shakier by the day, partly because the president is struggling against prostate cancer that has kept him in Europe for most of the past eight months. He returned to Kinshasa from his latest treatment on Friday.
Zaire Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo resigned late on Monday.
